To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIF-1 is a key regulator of postnatal lung growth, and HIF-1 expression is regulated by growth signals.
HIF-1 alpha is regulated by lung growth in dogs, and that HIF-3 alpha is regulated by both lung growth and pneumonectomy.
HIF-1 and EPO-R are upregulated in the growing lung, and the upregulation is regulated by the hypoxia inducible factor (HIF) system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the mechanisms that control lung development and regeneration.
understanding the molecular basis for lung growth and the potential for therapeutic manipulation of lung growth.
identifying mechanisms that regulate the growth of the mammalian lung.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HIF system is regulated in a manner that may be important for lung growth and that the HIF-1 system may play an important role in regulating EPO-R expression.
the HIF system is a potential regulator of EPO-R expression and that the HIF-1 and HIF-2 isoforms are involved in postnatal and post-PNX lung growth.
hypoxia-inducing factor (HIF) is regulated during postnatal and compensatory growth of lung.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIF-1 is upregulated and EPO-R is upregulated in the normal growing lung and in the lung that undergoes compensatory growth post-PNX.
the hypoxia-inducing factor system is a key regulator of postnatal and post-PNX lung growth.
HIF-1 alpha and EPO-R are regulated in parallel and that HIF- 1 alpha is a positive regulator of EPO-R.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HIF pathway plays a role in the regulation of lung growth and that this role is not restricted to hypoxic conditions.
HIF-1 is regulated in a manner that is consistent with the regulation of EPO, which is known to play a critical role in postnatal and post-PNX lung growth.
hypoxia is not the only factor involved in the regulation of HIF-2 alpha.
